claims.paraphrase: The Transformer is a sequence transduction model that drops recurrence and convolution entirely and relies only on attention to link input and output. The authors say it is the first such model.
On WMT 2014 English-to-German, Transformer (big) scores 28.4 BLEU, more than 2 BLEU above the best earlier result in the table, including ensembles (ConvS2S Ensemble, 26.36).
On WMT 2014 English-to-French, Transformer (big) scores 41.8 BLEU, a new single-model best, at about 2.3e19 training FLOPs. Note: Sec. 6.1 text on the same page says 41.0.

Even the base Transformer (27.3 BLEU on EN-DE, 3.3e18 FLOPs) beats every earlier model and ensemble listed for EN-DE, at a fraction of their training cost. It trained in about 12 hours on 8 P100 GPUs.
A self-attention layer connects every pair of positions with O(1) sequential operations and O(1) maximum path length, while a recurrent layer needs O(n) for both.

Self-attention costs O(n^2 d) per layer versus O(n d^2) for recurrence, so it is cheaper when sequence length n is smaller than representation size d, which the authors say is usual for sentence-level translation.

Dot products are divided by the square root of d_k. The authors suspect that without this, large d_k makes dot products large and pushes softmax into regions with tiny gradients. This is stated as a hypothesis, with a variance argument in a footnote.
With compute held constant, one attention head is 0.9 BLEU worse than the best setting on the dev set (24.9 vs 25.8), and quality also drops with too many heads (32 heads: 25.4).
Shrinking the attention key size d_k lowers quality (d_k 16: 25.1 BLEU; d_k 32: 25.4; base 64: 25.8), which the authors read as a sign that computing compatibility is not easy.

Learned positional embeddings give nearly the same result as the fixed sinusoidal encoding (25.7 vs 25.8 dev BLEU). Sinusoids were kept because they may extrapolate to longer sequences, which the paper does not test.
Bigger models score better and dropout helps avoid over-fitting: removing dropout drops dev BLEU from 25.8 to 24.6, and the big model reaches 26.4.

A 4-layer Transformer with little task tuning reaches 91.3 F1 (WSJ only) and 92.7 F1 (semi-supervised) on English constituency parsing. The authors say it beats all earlier models except the RNN Grammar, though Table 4 also lists a multi-task model at 93.0.
